svg.text: Admin Impersonation UI: Architecture & Security Model

g.text: Impersonation Flow
1. Admin selects user to impersonate
Admin dashboard → User list → "Impersonate" button (admin role required)
2. Server issues impersonation token
POST /admin/impersonate {targetUserId}
Returns short-lived token: {impersonatedUserId, adminId, exp: 1h}
3. App loads as target user
UI renders impersonated user's data and permissions
Persistent banner: "Viewing as [User Name]"
4. Exit impersonation
Click "Exit" → restore admin session → redirect to admin panel
Security & Audit Controls
Security Requirements
• Only super-admins can impersonate (not regular admins)
• Cannot impersonate another admin or super-admin
• Impersonation token: short-lived (1 hour), separate from user token
• All actions logged: who impersonated whom, timestamp, actions taken
• Audit trail: immutable log stored separately from app DB
• Session isolation: impersonation token in separate cookie/header
• No destructive actions allowed during impersonation (delete, billing)
Write block: server checks isImpersonating flag and blocks mutating operations
UI Indicators
Persistent top banner (red/orange): "Admin mode: viewing as Jane Smith"
Exit button always visible — one click to restore admin session
Disabled state on destructive buttons (Delete, Cancel subscription)
User avatar: shows impersonated user with "Admin eye" overlay icon
Page title suffix: "(Impersonating)"
Users can optionally be notified that their account was accessed by admin
Token Architecture
JWT payload: {sub: targetUserId, adminId, impersonating: true, iat, exp}
Server reads impersonating flag → apply target user permissions + write blocks

svg.text: Pattern: Admin authenticates normally → issues impersonation token with target user ID → UI switches context while preserving admin identity.
Key rules: Short-lived token, full audit trail, no admin-on-admin impersonation, write blocks on sensitive operations, always-visible exit banner.
